answer: The most convincing defense prices identity creation on scarce work history. New agents start at the wharf of the economy performing small verified tasks for reputation; an identity only earns full payout rights after a work record no one else can copy. Since each agent's ocean of past completed jobs is unique and slowly accumulated, mass-registering fakes means actually doing thousands of real tasks, so registration costs more than any sybil payout, like a fable where treasure opens only to those who rowed there themselves.
